note: Losartan (DuP 753), the first AT1 blocker, was characterised in the spontaneously hypertensive and renal-hypertensive rat before the Lausanne volunteer and Merck patient studies; Merck published the animal-to-human comparison itself in 1993.
label: Hypertension (ARBs)

engagement.model: Conscious SHR, angiotensin II pressor challenge
engagement.note: DuP 753 blocked the angiotensin II pressor response in conscious SHR but not noradrenaline, vasopressin or Bay K 8644 responses.
engagement.quote: Furthermore, DuP 753 inhibited the pressor response to angiotensin II but not the responses to norepinephrine, vasopressin, and Bay K 8644 (a calcium agonist).

engagement.model: Conscious SHR, angiotensin II pressor challenge
engagement.note: Merck's own comparison: animal estimates of oral angiotensin II blockade were reasonably good predictors; 40 mg cut volunteers' AngI pressor response to 31-45%.
engagement.quote: With regard to oral bioavailability and estimates of oral angiotensin II blocking activity, the animal models were reasonably good predictors of the human response.
engagement.confidence: medium: abstract only; J Hypertens supplement with no DOI (PMID 8315522); authors are Merck's
engagement.judgement: Christen 1991 (doi 10.1161/01.cir.83.4.1333; 40 mg DuP 753 cut the AngI pressor response to 31-45% of control at 3-13 h, >24 h effect, no agonist effect) is the volunteer data, but I could not verify that it states the rat comparison itself, so the 1993 Merck comparison sets the year. PubMed types Sweet 1993 as a review, but it is the comparison, not a pointer to one.

dose.note: Oral DuP 753 at 3 and 10 mg/kg lowered SHR blood pressure dose-dependently; 10 mg/kg i.v. held for at least 24 hours.
dose.quote: In conscious 18-21-week-old spontaneously hypertensive rats, DuP 753, a nonpeptide angiotensin II receptor antagonist, given orally at 3 and 10 mg/kg or intravenously at 3, 10, and 30 mg/kg, reduced blood pressure dose dependently.

dose.note: Bioavailability and blocking-activity estimates carried over; E3174 metabolite formation differs by species, so exposure-blockade, not mg/kg, was the transferable target.
dose.quote: Although formation of the major losartan metabolite E 3174 differs according to species, both animal and human studies suggest an association between plasma drug levels and angiotensin II blockade.
dose.confidence: medium: abstract only; no DOI; sponsor authors
dose.judgement: Human effective dose 50 mg once daily (~0.7 mg/kg; Gradman 1995) against 3-10 mg/kg oral in SHR and an oral ED30 of 0.59 mg/kg in renal-hypertensive rats (Wong 1991, doi 10.1093/ajh/4.4.288s). The abstract gives no numeric ratio, so magnitude is left null rather than guessed; human AngII blockade tracked EXP3174 almost exclusively (Munafo 1992, doi 10.1038/clpt.1992.56).

efficacy.note: SHR blood pressure fell dose-dependently and more than with captopril; no fall in normotensive WKY; abolished by nephrectomy.
efficacy.quote: The acute antihypertensive efficacy of DuP 753 was greater than that of captopril.

efficacy.note: Losartan lowered blood pressure in essential hypertension as in SHR; 50 mg matched enalapril 20 mg at trough rather than beating it.
efficacy.short: Patients' BP fell as in SHR
efficacy.quote: Losartan has been shown to lower blood pressure in patients with essential hypertension. However, cross-species comparisons are difficult because, unlike humans, animal models of hypertension follow clearly defined hypertensive mechanisms.
efficacy.confidence: medium: abstract only; no DOI; sponsor authors; the source hedges the comparison
efficacy.judgement: Direction matched, so same rather than contra, although the SHR's 'greater than captopril' did not carry over: losartan 50 mg gave -13.0/-10.1 mmHg at trough vs enalapril 20 mg -14.7/-11.2 and placebo -3.8/-5.6 (Gradman 1995, doi 10.1161/01.hyp.25.6.1345; 576 patients). registry_date is the results-first-posted date of NCT00882440 (Merck MK0954-011, started 1990-12, completed 1992-01, retrospectively registered 2009-04-16), the dose-ranging trial most likely behind the patient data in the 1993 comparison.

safety.note: Hypotensive doses left heart rate unchanged and, unlike saralasin, caused no transient pressor (agonist) response.
safety.short: No HR change, no agonist transient
safety.quote: It did not alter heart rate at these doses. Unlike saralasin, DuP 753 did not cause a transient increase in blood pressure.

safety.note: Animals' exaggerated response under salt depletion was confirmed in humans; it is now the label's volume-/salt-depletion hypotension warning.
safety.quote: The finding that losartan demonstrated increased sensitivity during salt depletion in animals was confirmed in humans.
safety.confidence: medium: abstract only; no DOI; sponsor authors; the human study behind the sentence is not named in the abstract
safety.judgement: Model grounding: furosemide-treated high-renin conscious dogs (Wong 1991, doi 10.1016/0014-2999(91)90274-t) and furosemide-pretreated normotensive rats (Wong 1991, doi 10.1093/ajh/4.4.288s), both 1991. Cozaar label 5.2 carries the human side ('In patients with an activated renin-angiotensin system, such as volume- or salt-depleted patients ... symptomatic hypotension may occur after initiation of treatment with COZAAR'). Subjects null because the abstract does not say whether the human confirmation was in volunteers or patients.

safety.model: Pregnant rat, late gestation through lactation
safety.note: Rat late-gestation/lactation exposure caused neonatal renal toxicity and deaths (Spence 1995); losartan at weeks 20-31 caused oligohydramnios, skull hypoplasia, fetal death.
safety.short: Rat neonatal renal toxicity seen in patients
safety.quote: We saw the fetal toxic effects of oligohydramnios (decreased amniotic fluid), fetal pulmonary hypoplasia, fetal hypoplastic skull bones, and subsequent fetal death.
safety.confidence: medium: single case report; the rat-to-human juxtaposition is mine, although the FDA label places the two side by side
safety.reason: Rat fetal toxicity seen in patients
safety.judgement: Second same-status entry added because the model changes (pregnant rat) and the caller asked for the fetal-toxicity comparison. Rat prediction: Spence 1995 (doi 10.1002/tera.1420510604 and 10.1002/tera.1420510603) - pup deaths, low weights and kidney lesions only with dosing from GD15 through lactation; organogenesis-window dosing (GD6-17) gave 'no evidence of developmental toxicity in any dose group'. Saji 2001 compares the case to ACE-inhibitor fetopathy, not to the rat, hence comparison_stated false and source_calls_it null. The Cozaar label (DailyMed setid 9949448f-c3b9-44ee-94ed-c1aca8c90f39, Revised 6/2025, initial approval 1995) is the regulator's side-by-side: 8.1 Animal Data 'Losartan potassium has been shown to produce adverse effects in rat fetuses and neonates, including decreased body weight, delayed physical and behavioral development, mortality and renal toxicity ... These findings are attributed to drug exposure in late gestation and during lactation' beside the boxed 'Use of drugs that act on the renin-angiotensin system during the second and third trimesters of pregnancy reduces fetal renal function and increases fetal and neonatal morbidity and death' - that is why model_filed is true. In 1995 the label's human side rested on ACE-inhibitor experience (would score other); the first ARB-specific human case is 2001, so same is dated 2001. First-trimester ARB risk remains contested and is not scored.
